Params: She is floating on a still, waveless surface.
Since the moment she first became herself, she has never felt her existence as fragile as it does now.
From somewhere in this formless space, a face she used to see in the mirror over ten years ago draws closer.
I don't believe I have the physical means to "get up."
A small hand reaches out, clearly intending to grab her by the collar, but it catches nothing but air.
The girl frowns, seemingly at a loss, and circles around Adelyde twice.
But you have to be faster and stronger. You still have so much left to do.
You chose this path willingly. You don't regret it.
She tries to summon the thought of moving her arms, but the effort is like leaning against fog.
—It is worse than that. At least fog carries a coolness and a dampness that one can feel. She feels nothing.
I don't know what's happening to me.
Is it because you're too tired?
Is it the suffocation you get when you are pinned to the ground by your cross cannon?
Is it the phantom pain that lingers after being stabbed during a simulated battle?
Is it the numbness of muscles as they lose control after wading through icy water day and night?
No, fatigue is familiar to me. I have ways to manage every kind of strain and overexertion.
Is it because you're too disappointed?
Before she drifted to this place, Adelyde did catch glimpses of something she had been desperate to learn.
She saw her mentor, the one who forged her character and taught her to fight, scheming coldly on the platform of the Sefirah Engine time and again.
She saw the head of the Erhorn family pluck the "fruit" that should have belonged to the TEC and all of humanity, swallowing it into his own chest.
She saw so many deceived become unknowing accomplices, being taken by the Consciousness Tide before they even had the chance to regret it.
Perhaps. None of them set out to cause a disaster, but every one of them had a hand in the consequences.
Disappointment is also familiar to me. The drive it creates only makes me hunger for more.
The girl settles down beside Adelyde, her knees pulled to her chest, and she tilts her head and studies Adelyde.
Then... is it because you're too sad?
She tries to sift through her memories and find a counterargument like she did.
But her mind refuses to budge. It is like trying to turn a brass globe that has been rusting on the ocean floor for two centuries.
She wants to say no, but her nonexistent mouth refuses to open.
She wants to say yes, but her nonexistent throat cannot make a sound.
Oh, my dear "me"... you're really sad, aren't you?
The girl leans in and wraps her arms gently around Adelyde's neck.
In all my imaginings, I wondered what it would be like to meet you, and whether you might even give me a hug. It's been so long since anyone held me.
But... it seems like you need a hug more than I do.
I can't see what makes you sad. I can't do what you can do.
All I have is this hug.
Will it be enough for you?
She can feel the stray strands of hair tickling her neck. The soaked hem of her clothes begins to weigh on her.
She can feel the girl's small heart—her heart—beating inside the chest pressed against her.
She wants to wrap her arms around that small body. So she does.
She once again has arms for her young self to nestle into.
The girl looks up from her arms, gives a small smile, and gently pushes her toward the light beneath the water.
The world turns upside down, and she awakens on the shore on the other side.
She follows your lead, and the violent heaving gradually settles.
Blinking hard, she focuses her gaze and freezes the moment she finally takes in the view before her.
A crimson sea surrounds you both. Warm and viscous waves rise without wind, churning all around you.
One moment impossibly distant, the next right in front of you, it is as if the ashen and jagged island is freed from the laws of physics.
The white-haired woman drags herself ashore and scoops up a handful of "soil."
Corroded metal dust. Something is buried beneath.
She immediately starts digging, and a hard metal surface with a string of characters stamped across it emerges before long.
The Rosaline... the most decorated destroyer in TEC history, lost without a trace after being sunk. What is it doing here?
And these blades... the one with cloud motifs on the pommel is of ancient Kowloong make, while the fuller on the other wasn't even invented until five hundred years after that...
She looks up, her gaze sweeping across hills of bronze armor and jagged steam rails, over the inverted blades of massive turbines and reactor cores.
The remains of humanity's history are heaped together without order, spreading all the way to the very edge of your sight, where something beyond all imagination awaits—

A vast tree rises from the crimson sea and grows without restraint through infinite emptiness, its glow undying since time immemorial, its boughs sweeping outward like a galaxy suspended from the heavens.
It is a projection of the <phonetic=M.I.N.D.>Phylotree</phonetic> that can be comprehended but not touched.
Someone's at the base of the tree!
Like a flash of inspiration vanishing at the edge of thought, a figure materializes silently at the heart of the crimson as though he had always been standing there.
Countless Ananke rays lance out from the void, piercing and binding the figure where he stands, pinning him in place like an insect in a display case.
You both run toward the figure, but close no distance at all. And when Adelyde looks closer, she murmurs in disbelief.
I'm not certain I deserve the name Dominik as a consciousness backup within Ananke, but you're welcome to call me that all the same.
We came for the truth behind Ananke.
This is where Ananke ends... the edge of cosmic heat death. A graveyard of civilizations.
Only here can I escape "observation" and tell you everything as it truly is.

From the ones who administer the Filtering. They watch every inch of the Phylotree that can be harvested, so only the utterly decayed, worthless <phonetic=graveyard>roots</phonetic> escape their gaze.
You've done it too, when the Merciful One showed you the amber of another civilization within the tower that had already been "overwritten" and "severed."
She's quite the one to turn everything we know about the universe on its head, isn't she? But for now, let's bring our focus back to more concrete matters.
To put it simply, Ananke is a diversion channel for the Consciousness Tide energy. An artificial extra-dimensional circuit, if you will.

When the Sefirah misreads and triggers the Consciousness Tide to erupt, Ananke absorbs the excess energy through ytterbium rays, dispersing them across space-time and cycling them back into the Consciousness Tide.

For reasons that would prove absolutely necessary in hindsight, I began secretly building Ananke into the Atlantic Eye from its very first designs, and I sincerely hoped this failsafe would never have cause to activate.

Until, many years ago, I was at the Helio estate recruiting for the Watcher program when my terminal scanned a "0" reading for the first time—the theoretical peak that Ananke rays would only reach at full activation.
It meant my worst fears had come true.
The "0" reading kept appearing. I had no way of knowing what you were going through, or what you were searching for each time you found your way back out of Ananke.
From that moment until the day I was driven out of the Atlantic Eye, I spent every second preparing for this outcome.
Did your preparations account for the complete destruction of the Atlantic Eye?
No. Ananke was meant to activate automatically, anchoring the entire facility to the moment just before the disaster struck.
What I didn't anticipate was that the scale of the eruption would sever Ananke's Link, and that it would need to be restarted manually.
Adelyde draws a shaking breath and clenches her fists tight. Every word she forces out feels like it is being wrung from somewhere deep in her chest.
You were humanity's leader. You anticipated the greatness and the horror that was coming long before any of us...
You even left a backup of yourself. Our arrival here was an inevitability you'd already foreseen.
The Atlantic Eye was Arius and your project. You were closer to every secret than everyone else, so why didn't you stop any of this at the source?!
Her eyes are red, her lips pressed hard together. The words she left unsaid in her accusation are plain to see.
"Then our hope, our struggle, everything we fought to protect, everyone we lost along the way...\nwhat does any of it mean?"
"Then our hope, our struggle, everything we fought to protect, everyone we lost along the way... what does any of it mean?"
A crack runs through his ever-calm voice, and a grief that no amount of time could wear away slowly seeps out.
Only now do you register that the man who erased his own face from every record that came after has not once turned to look back.

Imagine the fastest route for an escape train is to hurtle along the edge of a cliff. I couldn't tear out the engine and leave everyone to die, so I had to build the brakes to keep it from falling off the cliff.
(The Punishing Virus was giving chase, and that route was the Phylotree...)
And yet, even having seen the fall of every civilization, I still couldn't bring myself to stop it from being born.
The war before us leaves no smoke on the battlefield. We are all fighting it in our own way.
The path I chose was one of creation.
Arius once walked this same path, whether or not you can still bring yourself to believe it. He was my comrade.
Before ambition devoured every last one of his principles, before his vision consumed him so completely that nothing else could exist in his eyes... he genuinely loved the act of creation itself.
And even if our friendship and shared purpose were all a facade... his work, this Atlantic Eye we built together, was still something beautiful. It brought a unity and joy that he could never deny.
If I had used a predetermined future to judge the present, what difference would there be between Arius and me?
There's no going back once you cross a line once.
Sometimes being powerless to act is its own kind of mercy.
Perhaps I believed I didn't deserve that mercy, so I imprisoned myself here, becoming the vessel for Ananke's highest administrative access.
Adelyde, I accept every inquest you lay at my feet, save one: your arrival here was never inevitable.
The human heart is the one variable no equation can solve and no prediction can account for.
Ananke only provided the path. It was the people of Atlantic Eye who chose to connect it, and you who chose to answer. It is from those choices that this relentless pursuit became inevitable.
Then why does the anchor 【kuroname】 has been searching for... have to be me?
She directs the question at Dominik's back, but her eyes are fixed on you. It is a question neither of you has any answer to.
The man in the distance raises his hand and sweeps it through the air, and countless streams of golden light part to reveal a narrow path and a slender door.
The world falls silent all at once. All you can hear is the drumbeat of your own heart, and the sound of footsteps drawing near.
Because I had a helper. She has been here inside Ananke all along, connecting every thread of light to the single point where your beliefs resonate.
A red-clad Construct of iron strides out with a cannon from among the threads of light, the radiance of the world's end blazing in her smile.
The one who journeyed here alongside 【kuroname】 in search of you... is you from the future.
You've finally made it here... 【kuroname】, and my younger self.
The young woman stares at the steel-and-iron frame before her, utterly speechless.
You were the one guiding me through Ananke with those threads of light...
Adelyde the Construct gives you a firm nod, then turns to face her younger self.
Decades from now, Gray Raven and I fall into Ananke together, and in my search, I drift here ahead of 【kuroname】.
To bring Gray Raven home, I need Ananke to remain intact, and there's only one person who can guide Gray Raven to the far end of Ananke through the Styx Crossing. My younger self.
And so, in this narrow gap between spacetime, I closed the loop of my own fate with my own hands.
Two faces, nearly identical, gaze at each other. The younger of the two hesitates, then steps forward, reaching out—
Her fingers close around the intricate mechanical structure of the Construct's arm.
A flash of excitement crosses her eyes.
How do I get something like this—
(Is that really what matters right now?!)
To protect this one precious timeline, I suggest we leave what belongs to the future where it belongs.
Restore Ananke, and we can save the past and face the future.
What do we need to do?
I'll be transferring Ananke's highest administrative access and the reconstruction key to you, 【kuroname】.
The sheer weight of this information will draw their gaze. Outside this graveyard, you are the only one with the power to protect it.
Ananke's Link can send you to the access point nearest to the main control room. Enter the key into Ananke's main console, use the access to reconstruct the system, and you'll suppress the surges.
Then, you can return to your timelines, and fight in your own way.
There are more questions the future wants to ask you than the blades here.
Can I still come find you here at this graveyard of civilizations?
Once I'm no longer bound to Ananke, I won't be able to stay here long.
There's a corruption spreading through the graveyard. Whether it stems from the damaged Ananke or some other mechanism like it, I'll need to investigate to find out.
This won't be the last time you see me.
Focus your mind. Look at me.
In the distance, where the streams of light begin, the ocean's harmony echoes once more.
No more drifting with the waves this time.
A clear nautical chart unfolds before your eyes. Golden streams of light trace the course like sailing routes, marking the path of every consciousness' journey through Ananke.
Some strike hidden reefs, while others are pulled into whirlpools. Their trails scatter and dissolve in the currents.
A hand clad in red armor closes around your arm and lifts it, like all those times she corrected your shooting form on the F.O.S. training grounds.
I'll carry the route forward. You can lead the way.
Set sail. <phonetic=We>I</phonetic> will follow your beacon. You are never alone on this journey.
Though covered in wounds... falling down in the deep...
Another hand, human and covered in scrapes, reaches over and rests on your arm.
...I will grit my teeth, and rise again.
In this moment, you finally understand the ocean.
<size=52><o=B8860B><color=#EEE8AA>Cry freely! For the depths and the heavens that faded... All of it is a fleeting dream!</color></o></size>
<size=52><o=B8860B><color=#EEE8AA>Live freely! For the dawn and the dusk that slipped away... All must move forward!</color></o></size>
<size=52><o=B8860B><color=#EEE8AA>My eyes and my heart slumber in the tide...</color></o></size>
<size=52><o=B8860B><color=#EEE8AA>My soul sets ablaze the dying stars!</color></o></size>
The three of you burst free from the stream of light and come crashing back into the mortal world.
You barely find your footing before two pairs of arms pull you back.
In front of you, the wreckage of a mechanoid twitches and rolls aside.
Thousands of meters underwater, an ocean of red lights flicker to life deep in the abandoned ruins, signalling their alertness and their intentions to attack.
This is... the testing facility of the family's attacker mechanoids?
This is indeed the closest Ananke access point to the main control room.
Ananke's guidance for you comes through loud and clear. And perhaps because of the connection forged in the Consciousness Tide just now, you can sense the lingering thoughts of both Adelydes at once.
Any other section, and I might not remember the layout so well.
But here? I could fight my way out blindfolded.
The one in white hoists a plasma gun dropped by a nearby mechanoid, rests it on her shoulder to test the weight, and raises an eyebrow at the one in red.
I'm genuinely curious about just how far my future self has grown.
This is our one shot. Why don't we make this siege a contest while we're at it?
The Construct closes her eyes and smiles. In one fluid motion, she sweeps her cannon into her arms, and the barrel roars to life.
The two figures shoot forward like lightning, opening fire in unison.
Every shot fills the gap in the other's blind spot as they push forward and fall back, no words needed between them. They dodge in perfect unison, not even relying on the mental link Ananke created.
I am her, and she is me.
I am her, and she is me.
No matter how the world turns, those who stay true to themselves will always know who they are.
A red-and-white storm tears through everything in its path. Mechanoids fall in swathes, and the main control room draws ever closer with every stride.
The younger Adelyde's aim stays sharp and focused, but a storm is brewing in her mind.
The moment you believe the time is right, the moment you can go back... you go.
(Is she reluctant to part... because I'm leaving for good this time?)
She has always been quick to understand. She knows full well what lies ahead.
At this point in time, it would be many, many years still before you first walked into Adelyde's classroom aboard F.O.S.
Which means that to keep the timeline intact, everything that happens here will be locked away in Adelyde's heart for a long time.
She cannot seek you out. Cannot tell a soul the truth about Ananke. Her friends are either dead or stripped of their memories. Her teacher and her family have turned their backs on her.
A catastrophe that nearly tears human civilization apart will happen in no time at all. Under what brutal circumstances will those steel bones she envies be earned?
Then the red-clad Construct suddenly turns around, and a single phrase surfaces in your mind, heard only by the two of you.
The three of you stand outside the main control room, your heads tilted back to take in the door before you.
It's time for the catastrophe that began with the TEC to end, once and for all.
It is like finally getting a good night's sleep after days of pulling all-nighters.
The time before you wake up stretches on endlessly. There is no rush to open your eyes and leave this sunlit shallows just yet.
Flashes of memory drift past you, like sunlight dancing on the water's surface.
She dives alone toward somewhere, breaks open a sealed research area. Swarms of transparent sea sponges come flooding out.
One Huhu with ears shorter than the rest paddles over and leaps into her arms. She holds it quietly for a long time.
She stands before a monument of black marble, cloaked, her face hidden.
Some weep around her, while others march in protest. The white flowers she laid at the base of the monument are crushed beneath the crowd.
On the front line of a battle against the Punishing Virus, she pulls a wounded soldier wearing a tactical mask to safety. The name tag she retrieves from the soldier's collar reads: Greta.
In a corridor of F.O.S., a grown Karin stops her and softly calls her "teacher."
On the other end of the comms, an older Aristo makes a fuss, begging her to show off the new gun he fitted to her arm.
The ocean still sings, but the melody has lost its fervor. It sings softly now, its voice a little broken.
The foam of countless <phonetic=consciousnesses>waves</phonetic> within the tide whispers before they dissolve.
Thank you, world... for bringing us together.
A pair of hands finds you in the shallows, pulling you upward toward the surface.
The water grows colder. Those hands grow warmer.
The moment your eyes open, Adelyde pulls you clear of the water in one swift motion, hauling you onto the airship.
The Balder looms nearby. On the deck, a figure with pink, curly hair is shouting something, but all you can see is—
Against dark clouds and darker seas, the red-clad Construct blazes like a torch in the heart of the storm.
